fields.description: Proposed by the explicit out-of-scope section of epic sase-i1 plan at plans:202608/bead_search_regex.md; this is a pre-existing parity gap, not caused by the epic. Reproduction on master a3a536a03: compact bead search for No item with that key finds sase-i1.1 and sase-i2.2 through later lines in their notes but renders the first non-empty notes line, which does not contain the query; full output exposes the matching later line. Python _single_line_snippet selects the matching line, while Rust crates/sase_core/src/bead/cli.rs single_line_snippet preserves the older first-line behavior. Scope: make the shared/core compact renderer select the matching non-empty line without changing match semantics, add parity regression coverage, publish the core fix, and adopt the released floor in sase.

payload.close_reason: Backlog triage 2026-08-10: still reproduces but deprioritized out of the top seven. Confirmed at sase-core master: crates/sase_core/src/bead/cli.rs single_line_snippet still does value.lines().next() while Python _single_line_snippet (src/sase/bead/cli_query.py:520) picks the matching line. The gap is display-only — match semantics are identical and the matching line is still visible in full output — so this is a cosmetic parity nit whose fix costs a core change, a publish, and a floor bump. Reopen with a +1 if compact search output actually misleads someone during triage.
